dse_runs.notes: Spec: 32 requests per 1us tick, all results within 0.44us p99, min LUTs+FFs. From memory: pipelined_m dominated the front on the similar bursty spec (m=4..7, dw=15..20, n_iter=12..13); pipelined (dw 15..18, n_iter 14..16) reached the front on the 1/cycle DDS spec; iterative can't hit 1/cycle; unrolled_k never reached a front. L1 analytic p99 under-predicts simulated p99 ~1.4-1.5x, so keep margin on sys_p99_batch_us <= 0.44us.

final_text:
Campaign complete — the single spec **multiaxis_control** is finalized.

**Summary:** L1 (structured DSE, all 400 evals, 30-design front) found pipelined_m m=2 designs dominating the front for the 32-requests-per-tick batch spec; L2 SimPy simulation confirmed all top-5 designs pass the p99 ≤ 0.44 µs batch-latency constraint (simulated 0.243–0.249 µs, with the L1 analytic bound under-predicting by only ~2.5% — far less than the ~1.4–1.5× seen on the bursty spec). L3/L4 had no recorded measurement rows for this design (fresh RTL run too heavy for W=19; L4 not run live), so L5 back_annotate had no measured data to compare and flagged no winner change — no reexplore needed. **Final selection: `pipelined_m:data_width=19, n_iter=14, angle_guard=-1, frac_guard=2, rounding=trunc, m=2`** — estimated 1417 LUTs+FFs (909 LUT / 507 FF), 12.4 accuracy bits (max abs err 2⁻¹²·⁴⁴), 164 MSPS throughput, simulated p99 batch latency 0.243 µs. Lesson stored for future campaigns.
